svg.text: The inviscid shell model has the exact self-similar solution u_k(t) = (1/3) 2^(-k) (T - t)^(-1).
Its vorticity a_k = 2^k u_k = (1/3)(T - t)^(-1) is FLAT in k, so the local exponent is 0 at every shell and the jitter is exactly zero.
Both panels show shell k against time t, height = vorticity level. Left: the exact solution. Right: the same explosion with a frozen jitter profile riding on it.
height = 1/(1 - t), clipped at t = 0.9 T; the level diverges at T

The profile is a perfect power law at every instant, so the jitter is exactly zero: what explodes is the LEVEL, not the shape. The right panel's frozen jitter keeps the same shape while the level diverges.
The lesson of the pair: during an explosion the jitter does not grow, shrink, or decide anything. It cannot cause the blow-up and cannot prevent it — only the level moves.

Honest limits: left panel exact, right panel's roughness synthetic. This is the untruncated inviscid model — our truncated model provably cannot blow up at all, and the flat profile makes the enstrophy diverge at every time.
